item.description: Manchester City have moved to the top of the Premier League. Rayan Cherki's late goal secured them a 2-1 victory at Nottingham Forest. Advertisement

item.title: Grimley steps away from Armagh team
item.description: Niall Grimley has announced his decision to step away from the Armagh football panel for 2026. The Madden clubman was a key part of the 2024 All Ireland winning squad and helped his club to a county championship this season. The midfielder refused to rule out a return but won't be making himself available for the foreseeable due to family reasons. Advertisement

item.title: Jack Kennedy takes Grade One win in Leopardstown
item.description: Gordon Elliott won four out of the seven races won at Leopardstown this afternoon. The pick of the results for the County Meath trainer was Paddy Power Chase which went the way of Favouri De Champdou. That was one of a hattrick for jockey Sam Ewing who was also on board Solness in the Grade One Paddy's Rewards Club Chase and Hardy Stuff in the opener. item.title: Littler and Bunting in action in the Ally Pally tonight
item.description: The PDC World Darts Championship has resumed after the Christmas break, with reigning champion Luke Littler among the players in third-round action. Littler will take on the veteran Mensur Suljovic in the last match of the night at Alexandra Palace. Already today, Krzysztof Ratajski came from 3-1 down to beat Wesley Plaisier 4-3. Advertisement Meanwhile, Luke Woodhouse booked his spot in the next round with a 4-1 victory over Andrew Gilding.

item.title: Dingle business owners and community lay on packed calendar of events this Christmas and New Year
item.description: Businesses and community groups in Dingle have put together a packed calendar of events this Christmas and New Year's period to attract people to the area. Community organiser Richie Williams says they decided to offer a full programme because two weekends fall during the holidays. These events are on top of a range of Christmas Day swims around the Dingle peninsula and the world famous Lá an Dreoilín on St Stephen's Day. item.title: Shortage of supply was the main factor in Kerry housing market this year
item.description: The shortage of supply of housing in Kerry is still the major factor in the housing market here. That’s the view of Kerry auctioneer Paul Stephenson, of Sherry Fitzgerald Stephenson Crean. He said plenty of people in Kerry have the finance to buy houses, but the supply just isn’t there. Advertisement He said the market was very strong in 2025, but the lack of supply is still the driving factor.
